subject.title: Feature Request: Add cumulative history search and multi-account support

question: Should Wacrawl prioritize a profile-scoped cumulative archive, a read-only federated search over existing snapshots, or retain point-in-time restore as the supported historical workflow?
rationale: The current replacement-based archive model cannot meet the acceptance criteria without choosing persistent identity, deduplication, storage growth, restore, and CLI UX semantics; this is product architecture rather than a narrow defect repair.

options.title: Split and design cumulative history first
options.body: Define an account-independent snapshot provenance and deduplication contract first, then track multi-account profile isolation as a separate follow-up.

options.title: Build one profile-aware archive program
options.body: Adopt profile namespaces, profile-scoped backup state, and cumulative history together, accepting a larger schema and migration program.

options.title: Keep snapshot restore only
options.body: Document point-in-time restore to an alternate `--db` as the supported recovery path and decline aggregate-history behavior for now.

recommendation.title: Split and design cumulative history first
recommendation.body: Define an account-independent snapshot provenance and deduplication contract first, then track multi-account profile isolation as a separate follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: The current snapshot and media backup model was introduced through their merged work, so they are the strongest available routing candidate for its future boundary.
